Physics-Informed Machine Learning for Cross-Surface Generalization in Droplet Impact Prediction

Parth Sharma  ·  Kshitij Dhariwal  ·  Prabal Kaushik
Thapar Institute of Engineering & Technology, Patiala, Punjab, India
Problem
Physics
Data
ML Model
Results
Conclusion
01
Why Droplet Fate Matters
  • Whether an impacting droplet rebounds or pins is foundational to anti-icing coatings and microelectronic spray cooling.
  • Classical dimensionless scaling — Reynolds, Weber, Ohnesorge — is interpretable but generalizes poorly across complex, heterogeneous functionalized surfaces.
  • Raw-parameter ML (velocity, diameter) risks entangling scale with surface identity, degrading on unseen topographies.
  • This work tests — rather than assumes — whether physics-informed dimensionless features improve out-of-distribution generalization over a raw-parameter baseline.
02
Surface Engineering & Interfacial Physics
  • Laser-textured superhydrophobic aluminium substrates replicate the lotus-leaf Cassie–Baxter state for rapid rebound.
  • High-velocity impact can force liquid into micro-cavities — a transition toward a pinned, wetted Wenzel-like state.
  • Discrete geometry (channel spacing, depth) resists smooth empirical fitting — motivating a learned mapping of We–Re–Oh × topography → terminal droplet state.

03
Experimental Dataset — Može et al.
  • Public dataset — Može et al., University of Ljubljana (Mendeley Data, DOI 10.17632/wsh8rxwd38).
  • 1,498 impacts on laser-textured superhydrophobic Al alloy 1050A-H24 (channel depth 6/25 µm; spacing 50–800 µm; FDPA-monolayer treated).
  • +125 impacts on a smooth, chemically identical reference surface (REF-H) — held out entirely for out-of-distribution testing.
  • Water–glycerol mixtures, 0–91 wt.% glycerol (two orders of magnitude in viscosity); droplets released from five heights to vary impact velocity.

04
Physics-Informed vs. Raw-Parameter Models
  • Regression target: maximum spreading factor — the one dynamic outcome measured identically on both surface types (rebound efficiency and contact time are reported only for textured surfaces, absent from REF-H).
  • Two XGBoost feature sets compared — Dimensionless: Re, We, Oh + channel spacing & depth. Raw baseline: diameter, velocity, ρ, σ, μ + same geometry descriptors.
  • Both train on the 1,498 textured experiments; evaluated in-distribution (20% hold-out) and on the full 125-sample REF-H set.
  • SHAP values computed on the dimensionless model to test physical grounding.

Dimensionless features reduce absolute error in both settings — but do not degrade proportionally less. Physical scaling constrains the model’s reasoning without, by itself, guaranteeing transfer to a qualitatively different surface.

06
Key Findings
01
Lower absolute error, both settings
Dimensionless RMSE beats the raw baseline in-distribution and on REF-H alike (0.0275 vs. 0.0331; 0.0800 vs. 0.0931).
02
Comparable relative degradation
ID→OOD error growth is similar for both models (191.5% vs. 181.0%) — scaling alone doesn’t guarantee proportionally better transfer.
03
Physically grounded reasoning
SHAP identifies Weber number as the dominant driver, consistent with established capillary–inertial scaling.
04
Geometry descriptors: an incomplete proxy
Channel spacing/depth alone don’t capture the wetting mechanism — trapped-air fraction, Cassie–Baxter ↔ Wenzel — that separates textured from smooth surfaces.
07
Discussion, Conclusion & Future Work
An honest, mixed result
Dimensionless feature engineering improves absolute accuracy and preserves physical interpretability — but does not, alone, resolve out-of-distribution generalization to an entirely novel surface geometry. Both models degrade substantially on REF-H, suggesting channel spacing and depth alone are an incomplete proxy for the underlying wetting mechanism.
Speaks to the conference’s Wetting & De-wetting and Impact of Droplets onto Surfaces themes
Future work
  • Incorporate wetting-state-aware features (e.g., trapped-air fraction).
  • Explicit geometry embeddings in place of scalar channel descriptors.
  • Dimensional analysis constrains a model’s reasoning — it does not, by itself, guarantee transfer across qualitatively different wetting regimes.
